whatItIs.text: Sesame seeds ground into a pourable paste — the base of hummus, baba ghanoush, halva, and countless dressings; the name comes from Arabic for 'to grind'.

historyNote.text: Sesame's oldest mention is a cuneiform document 4,000 years old describing sesame wine served to the gods; a 10th-century Arabic cookbook gives a ground-sesame condiment, and tahini appears in a 13th-century hummus recipe — English only picked the word up in the late 1930s.

howToChoose.text: Choose smooth, pourable tahini of hulled, roasted seeds; unhulled is more bitter. Stir before judging — separated oil is normal, bitterness is not.

storage.text: Keep sealed in a cool cupboard or fridge; the fridge stiffens it, so stir and warm slightly before use.

useItUp.text: Whisk with lemon juice and water into a sauce for everything from falafel to roasted squash; it also thickens smoothies and makes halva-adjacent fudge with honey.
